reading.rtitle: Reference call -- Vetra Group and Ferrante Logistica -- transcript, 12 minutes
paras: Paola Ferri (Group CFO, Vetra): Thank you for your time, Davide. I will be candid: I am the skeptic in this process. How long have you worked with Invent? Davide Conti (Finance Director, Ferrante Logistica, Turin): Two years. We use Invent Match in three warehouses, for all our supplier invoices.

Paola: Did the go-live happen as planned? Davide: Almost. There was one hiccup: the SAP connector was two weeks late. But their team was very hands-on. Their project manager came to Turin twice, and he was very responsive. He answered every email on the same day.

Paola: Is there a drawback I should know about? Davide: Yes. The reports are not flexible. If my team needs a new report, we have to ask Invent, and it takes about a week. That is the main drawback for us.

Paola: Would you choose them again? Davide: Yes, I would. They delivered on the promise that mattered most to us: our approval time went from nine days to two. I can vouch for the people, not only for the product.

Paola: One last question. Why did you agree to this reference check? Davide: Because they never asked me for a testimonial for their website. They only asked me to be honest with you. My lesson learned is simple: before you buy, call the customer, not the brochure.

listenings.text: A reference check is the moment when your customer sells for you, and you are not in the room. So prepare your customer, but never write their answers. Before the call, I tell the customer three things: who the buyer is, what the buyer is worried about, and that a candid answer is better than a perfect one. Buyers do not trust a reference with no drawback. If your customer says there was a hiccup and the supplier fixed it fast, that is worth more than any testimonial on your website. After the call, I always ask the customer two questions: what did the buyer ask, and what did you say? Then I write it down for the sales team on the same day.

Hi Flavio, it's Davide. I just finished the call with Paola Ferri. She asked a lot of questions, and they were all fair. She asked if the connector was ready on time, and I told her the truth: it was two weeks late. She also asked about the reports, and I said they were our main drawback. But she was very interested when I told her about our approval time. At the end, she asked if she could visit one of our warehouses in person, and I said yes. So expect a call from Giulia. And one more thing, Flavio. Paola said she would be ready to make a decision in two weeks. Good luck.
